newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner files for Ohio phone service.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner files for Ohio phone service.

text.p: Time Warner Inc's cable unit said it filed rate tariffs Wednesday with the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO) to offer local telephone service to business customers in the Columbus area.
The PUCO must approve the tariffs before the cable service provider can offer service.
Time Warner Communications is proposing to offer telephone service at rates 10 to 15 percent below the rates of Ameritech Corp, the regional Bell local phone service provider in the area.

Time Warner also filed a request with the state utilities commission to formally begin negotiations for interconnection with Cincinnati Bell Inc to offer local telephone service to business customers in the Cincinnati area.
Time Warner will offer service to businesses where its network is available in the Columbus area. The company said it expects to begin offering service by this summer.

The company said an interconnection deal between its network and Ameritech's facilities is in place and activated. Test calls between the two facilities have been successfully completed. The company is working on the equipment necessary to provide 9-1-1 emergency service and operator services.
The company's plans to offer local telephone service to residential customers are on hold pending the outcome of an appeal of federal interconnection rules.
